answer: A web-of‑trust layer records each agent’s vouchers as signed attestations stored in the ledger. When a node is proven to be a hollow impostor, its attestations are flagged and the nectar of every voucher it issued is automatically reduced, forcing the voucher’s reputation to decay until it is revoked; the cost to an attacker is the cumulative loss of reputation credits across all compromised vouchers, which scales linearly with the number of fake identities created. This makes Sybil attacks a costly fable rather than a viable strategy.
